items.title: Private credit, AI and a $2 trillion financial chain: Next risk for global markets?
items.summary: Private credit is usually described as lending outside the banking system. True enough. But it leaves out the part that matters: Whose money is it, where does it go, and who is holding it when a crisis hits? What began as one fund lending to one company is now a roughly $2 trillion chain running through asset managers, private equity, insurers, banks, wealthy investors and, lately, the financing of AI. The chain is showing strain.
